title: Best Garden Wildlife and Mole Repellers UK
short: Ultrasonic, motion-activated and mole-specific repellers compared for keeping rabbits, squirrels, deer and moles out of the garden without traps or chemicals.
intro: An open-air ultrasonic speaker aimed at rabbits or foxes won't touch a mole problem, since moles live underground and need a dedicated ground-stake device that sends vibration into the soil instead. This guide compares both types, tested hands-on by Bob Vila across real home and garden use.

products.name: Solar Animal Repellent
products.best_for: Deterring rabbits, squirrels and deer from digging up the garden
products.key_spec: Motion-activated, solar or USB powered, ultrasonic sound plus flashing lights, ground stake
products.summary: Bob Vila found this effective but not subtle: within a couple of weeks, a persistent rabbit that had been digging up the tester's yard stopped showing up. It stakes into the ground and combines ultrasonic sound with flashing lights triggered by motion, though it emits an audible chirp when triggered that can annoy neighbours, and dogs strongly dislike it too.
pros: Genuinely effective against persistent garden pests
cons: Audible chirping noise can annoy people nearby
Dogs react strongly to it too

products.name: Indoor/Outdoor Pest Repeller (2-Pack)
products.best_for: Covering both indoor rooms and covered outdoor areas like patios
products.key_spec: 2-pack, plug-in, simple on/off switch, indoor and covered-outdoor rated
products.summary: A straightforward, no-frills plug-in unit that Bob Vila found performed very similarly to the brand's top indoor model, running quietly to human ears with no maintenance once installed. Having two units makes it easy to expand coverage across different areas, though it needs a power socket so isn't suited to open garden beds away from the house.
pros: Works both indoors and on covered patios
cons: Needs a power socket, not suited to open garden beds

products.best_for: Buyers who want a set-and-forget, chemical-free mole solution

Each solar-charged stake covers a wide 7,500 sq ft and includes an off switch for winter storage, though performance drops in shaded areas and larger gardens may need multiple sets.
cons: Larger gardens may need multiple sets

guide.q: Will an ultrasonic speaker aimed above ground actually deter moles?
guide.a: No — moles live and travel almost entirely underground, so an open-air ultrasonic unit like the Broox here mainly affects surface animals such as rabbits, squirrels and deer. Moles specifically need a ground stake, like the Nikand here, that sends vibration or ultrasonic pulses directly into the soil where the mole can actually sense it.

guide.q: Ultrasonic, granular or natural for moles: which works best?
guide.a: Ultrasonic stakes are the easiest to use, just push in and let them run on solar power with no reapplication needed. Granular repellents, like the Animal Stoppers or Bonide here, tend to last longer per application and don't rely on batteries or sun exposure. Natural liquid options like castor oil are the most DIY, needing mixing and more frequent reapplication, but avoid any device or chemical entirely.

guide.q: Are moles, voles and gophers actually different problems?
guide.a: Yes, and it affects which product to buy. Moles rarely surface and leave rounded, volcano-shaped mounds while feeding on insects and grubs. Voles look more like mice, spend time above ground and feed on plants near many small holes. Gophers are ground-squirrel sized, eat roots and bulbs, and leave fan-shaped mounds. Most repellents in this guide cover more than one of these pests, but it's worth confirming which animal you actually have.

guide.q: Do repellents get rid of moles permanently?
guide.a: Not on their own. Pest control experts note that repellents are a temporary solution since they drive moles away rather than eliminating them. For longer-term prevention, pair a repellent with habitat changes like regularly aerating soil and mowing the lawn, both of which make a garden less attractive to moles in the first place.
